items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Thoreau said, ‘A man’s well can be gauged in terms of the things he doesn’t need.’ I don’t need what you have.

ctx.x: Yeah. He was a little . . . He felt the business had passed him by. Didn’t get his just desserts, I think he felt. He had so much worship. Bix had the same thing. Couldn’t understand the difference between worship from musicians and total indifference from the public. They couldn’t get the idea that you’re playing for an uneducated mass of people, musically uneducated. It’s tough to swallow that. It’s very difficult to have been at the very peak of your profession and then come down.

I’ve told people who see the way I live. I have friends who live . . . oh my God. 3500 square feet houses. This house would about fit into the servant’s wing. They say, “Jesus. You like this.” I say, “I like what it gives me. I have freedom. Thoreau said, ‘A man’s well can be gauged in terms of the things he doesn’t need.’ I don’t need what you have. Your overhead’s killing you. You’ve got to keep doing that crap.” They know it. Walter Matthau. Fine actor. “What are you doin’, Walter?” “Looking for a job.” The…
What’s the story of this famous old Rolls Royce that you used to travel in?
